# Native runtime benchmark

The Windows/macOS/Linux portable benchmark uses this same EYS v2 project.
71 targets cover normal dialogue/portraits/transitions, isolated effects,
particles, audio/video, player panels and combined stress. The suite adds
runtime sleep/wake and resolution/fullscreen cases. See `dev/docs/testing.md`.

Assets are generated by `dev/scripts/benchmark-fixtures.sh` (FFmpeg and cwebp).
They contain no external game artwork or recordings and use the repository
license. Backgrounds: 1920×1080 WebP q80; transparent figures: 720×1440 lossless
WebP; stereo audio: 48 kHz Ogg Opus; video: 1920×1080/24fps H.264 baseline plus
AAC; LUT: horizontal 16 slices. Tracked media is shared across platforms;
CI does not regenerate it. Generated calibration textures exercise real
production paths; they do not represent every game's artistic/compression mix.

The opening is the no-effect reference; other scenes are selected by `perf
--timeline bench_*`. They deliberately do not connect as a playable story.
Samples keep normal runtime owners; no copied renderer or fake CPU workload.
Changing assets or workload parameters invalidates comparison with old runs.

Example: `keine perf <project> --timeline bench_particle_layers_768 --mode
continuous --raw`. Pack with `keine bundle <project> --benchmark --output <dir>`.
The encrypted package also includes the publisher's isolated I/O stress data.
Missing targets or failed workloads make the report incomplete, not successful.
